value_disputes.issue: Regulatory permission vs. carbon efficiency and demographic/financial feasibility trade-offs.
value_disputes.framing: Zoning assigns a high score due to permitted use status, while demographic, pro_forma, and sustainability analysts weigh moderate market fit and environmental benefits against site constraints.

value_disputes.issue: Regulatory prohibition versus high environmental sustainability.
value_disputes.framing: Zoning heavily penalizes the typology due to a blank/not permitted use status, whereas the sustainability analyst assigns a high score based on multi-unit density advantages.

value_disputes.issue: As-of-right zoning permission versus low baseline prevalence in existing housing stock.
value_disputes.framing: Zoning finds a clear permitted path, while the demographic analyst scores lower due to limited regional representation of attached single-family structures.

value_disputes.issue: Regulatory uncertainty regarding overlays versus demographic alignment with smaller household configurations.
value_disputes.framing: Zoning gives a low score due to the absence of the ADU overlay on the site, whereas the demographic analyst gives a higher score based on trends favoring smaller household footprints.

value_disputes.issue: Special exception zoning hurdles and higher construction costs versus demographic need and sustainability benefits.
value_disputes.framing: Zoning and pro_forma highlight regulatory hurdles (special exception) and high R-4 construction costs, while demographic and sustainability analysts favor the typology due to local senior population shares and multi-unit efficiency.

value_disputes.issue: High regulatory alignment and historical stock prevalence versus poor environmental sustainability performance.
value_disputes.framing: Zoning and demographic analysts reward the typology for matching historical patterns and permitted use status, while the sustainability analyst penalizes it for higher per-unit carbon and car dependency.
